Algorithms

Step-by-step methods for sorting, searching and finding routes, and how to compare them.

How does a map app find the quickest route so fast?

Practise this subject in Algo Archipelago

Foundations

  • What an algorithm isA set of clear steps that solves a problem, what makes a good one, and Euclid's method for the greatest common divisor as a first example.
  • Maths you needThe few pieces of maths that algorithm analysis uses, sums, powers and logarithms, with small examples.
  • The RAM computational modelThe simple model of a computer that algorithm analysis uses, where basic steps each count as one.
  • Analysing algorithmsHow to describe how an algorithm's work grows with the size of its input, using growth rates and Big-O.

Basic methods

  • Brute forceThe simplest way to solve a problem, trying everything, shown with sorting and with counting the pairs of points.
  • RecursionHow a problem can be solved by solving smaller copies of itself, with factorials, Fibonacci numbers and the Tower of Hanoi.

Graphs

  • Graph conceptsWhat a graph is, the words used to describe one, and two ways to store it in a computer.
  • Graph traversalTwo ways of visiting every vertex of a graph, depth-first and breadth-first, and how their orders differ.

Decrease and conquer

  • Decrease and conquer by a constantSolving a problem by reducing it by one step at a time, shown with insertion sort and ordering tasks by their dependencies.
  • Decrease and conquer by a factorSolving a problem by cutting it down by a fraction each step, shown with binary search and fast powers.

Greedy methods and limits

  • Greedy methodsHow picking the best-looking choice at each step can give a perfect answer, and the cases where it does not.
  • Minimum spanning treesHow to connect every point in a network with the least total cost, using Kruskal's greedy method.
  • Hard problems: P and NPWhy some problems have no known fast solution, what P and NP mean, and what to do when you meet one.
